surprise: FoX forget gates (Lin et al. 2025) on the 4 positional heads of the 115-fable hybrid (per-block Linear(256,4) gates, zero-init weights and bias logit(exp(-slope)) so the run starts as exactly 115's ALiBi; 4 NoPE heads untouched; 4,806,168 params, i.e. 115's 4,800,000 + 6,168, not the 4,802,584 mis-added in params.json) scored 474/579/571 on seeds 0/1/2 vs 115's 639/646/609: exact means 541.00 vs 631.33, -90.3, paired -165/-67/-38, every seed down and outside the registered -45..+45 range. Discard. The registered mechanism is REFUTED in direction, and it failed the same way 113's steep slopes did: the data-dependent decay learned on cap-6 chains over-localises at unseen lengths. Round-1 targets solved 252/548/329 vs 115's 718/756/691, round-1 sample acc 0.087/0.182/0.092 vs 0.318/0.301/0.315, round-1 parse failures 24655/19392/25053 of 48,000 = 51/40/52% vs 25/22/18% (113: 50/30/64%), so at T=0.8 the gated model emits malformed 7+-line chains twice as often as the fixed-slope incumbent, while cap-6 held-out greedy is only ~1 point lower (0.972/0.969/0.969 vs 0.9815/0.983/0.9845): a length-extrapolation failure, not underfitting. Expert iteration then repairs it from the verifier signal, as in 113: seeds 1/2 cleared the parse failures by round 2 (5785/5677 = 12%) and reached r4 1030/1052 (115: 1122/1065), but seed 0 stayed collapsed for three rounds (parse failures 50/45% at r2/r3, targets 340/639) and only cleared at r4 (11%, 923), which is where its -165 comes from; r1->r4 gains +671/+482/+723 are catch-up, not a property of the gates. The eval frontier moved down on every seed: ge10 55/81/69 vs 103/97/89, ge11 5/16/14 vs 25/23/19, ge12 1/4/2 vs 5/4/4, L* 11 (115: 12/11/11); per-bin 7: 0.45/0.49/0.57 vs 0.62/0.63/0.58, 10: 0.23/0.30/0.25 vs 0.36/0.34/0.32, 11: 0.08/0.25/0.25 vs 0.41/0.39/0.31; whole-run Lean-gate parse failures 88214/45892/50441 of 266,912 (33/17/19%). Second surprise, a systems one: pretraining ran at exactly HALF of 115's throughput, 2078/2070/2079 steps vs 4204/4218/4263 (-51%; the registration predicted -5% to -25%; 116-fable's grad-carrying shared table cost 18%). Each block now builds a (B, 8, T, S) bias that requires grad, so SDPA cannot use the fused kernel and the bias build, cast and backward run six times per step; RL decoding was unaffected (238-316 samples/s vs 256-313; rounds 247-330 s; totals 1639/1832/1769 s). The halved step count cost no fit: final val loss 0.0863/0.0801/0.0809 vs 0.0826/0.0806/0.0792, minima 0.0799/0.0777/0.0775 vs 0.0778/0.0793/0.0777 (115 at step 2201 already had 0.0843; the wall-clock cosine, not the step count, sets the endpoint), so the fewer steps are a confound for the round-1 collapse only through less schedule time at high LR, which 111/113 (4,700/4,200 steps, similar val) argue is not what drives the 7+-line start. Omission: the registration promised a final-gate diagnostic (mean log f per head) that the code never logged, so the direction the gates moved (presumably steeper than the init slopes) is inferred from the collapse, not measured. Lessons: across 116-fable (T5-bucketed table, +3), 116-claude (learned per-block slopes, +3) and this run (-90), the positional heads' distance prior is at a local optimum under 115's fixed table: static reshaping buys nothing and content-dependence learned from cap-6 statistics hurts, so the next ideas should leave the positional mechanism alone. If content-dependent decay is ever retried it needs (a) a fused kernel (FlexAttention score_mod with a cumsum bias) and (b) a length-safe parametrisation, e.g. gates that can only OPEN relative to the ALiBi slope (log f >= -slope) so the decay can never exceed the fixed prior that 115 showed extrapolates.
